proposals.title: Spatial Domain Clustering with Integrated Denoising
proposals.summary: This proposal aims to create a clustering framework that not only segments spatial transcriptomics data into biologically meaningful domains but also integrates denoising directly into the process. The method leverages spatially aware clustering techniques that incorporate local transcriptomic information and noise models, ensuring that the resulting clusters maintain sharp boundaries while mitigating technical variability. By directly integrating denoising into the clustering step, the analysis seeks to enhance spatial domain accuracy and support subsequent integration with multi-sectional and 3D tissue analyses.

proposals.title: Adaptive Boundary-Aware Smoothing for Enhanced Signal Recovery
proposals.summary: This analysis proposes an adaptive smoothing algorithm specifically designed to reduce noise without compromising the integrity of tissue boundaries. By dynamically tuning smoothing parameters based on local gene expression variability and spatial context, the method preserves sharp transitions between heterogeneous domains. The technique also facilitates improved segmentation and further downstream integration, making it well-suited for complex tissue architectures and potential multi-section comparisons.

proposals.title: Graph-Based Denoising with Boundary Sensitivity
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on applying graph-based diffusion methods tailored to spatial transcriptomics data. By constructing a graph where nodes represent spots and edges encode spatial proximity, the approach diffuses gene expression information while explicitly preserving boundary information. Special attention is given to modulating the diffusion process near sharp transitions, thus ensuring effective denoising that respects intrinsic tissue architecture and aids in precise domain delineation.

proposals.title: 3D Tissue Reconstruction via Serial Section Integration
proposals.summary: Targeting the challenge of integrating data from consecutive tissue sections, this proposal outlines methods to reconstruct three-dimensional tissue architecture. The approach involves correcting section-specific artifacts and aligning spatial expression data across serial slices. By emphasizing both spatial domain accuracy and inter-sectional consistency, the analysis aims to produce a coherent 3D model of tissue organization, which can serve as a basis for further studies on tissue gradients and transitions.

proposals.title: Spatially-Informed Dimensionality Reduction for Domain Recovery
proposals.summary: This analysis introduces an enhanced dimensionality reduction technique that incorporates spatial constraints alongside gene expression data. The goal is to produce a low-dimensional representation that faithfully reflects tissue domains and preserves boundary information. By embedding spatial proximity into the reduction process, the method addresses issues of fragmented domains and facilitates both improved denoising and subsequent cross-sectional integration, preparing the data for more robust downstream analyses.

proposals.title: Comparative Multi-Resolution Analysis of Domain and Boundary Features
proposals.summary: This proposal evaluates the impact of varying spatial resolutions, from multicellular spots to nearly single-cell beads, on the integrity of domain segmentation and boundary detection. By systematically comparing datasets acquired at different resolutions, the analysis aims to identify resolution-dependent artifacts and optimize computational strategies for both denoising and domain delineation. In addition, insights from these comparisons may guide best practices for integrating datasets from heterogeneous platforms.

proposals.title: Transitional Zone Detection and Characterization
proposals.summary: Focused on regions where tissue properties shift gradually, this proposal develops methods to detect and analyze transitional zones within tissues. Utilizing gradient analysis combined with clustering, the approach delineates regions of smooth transitions from areas with sharp boundaries. Such characterization enhances our understanding of cellular interactions and tissue organization while also providing a targeted framework for addressing noise and inconsistencies in areas key to spatial domain definition.

proposals.title: Robust Feature Extraction for Cross-Sectional Alignment
proposals.summary: This analysis is designed to extract invariant spatial features that facilitate the alignment and integration of data across tissue sections. By focusing on features robust to technical noise and platform variability, the method enhances cross-sectional integration and supports the reconstruction of continuous tissue domains in 3D space. The approach underlines the importance of maintaining boundary accuracy and smooth transitions across different sections.

proposals.title: Normalization Framework for Heterogeneous Spatial Datasets
proposals.summary: This proposal outlines a comprehensive normalization strategy to harmonize spatial transcriptomics data collected under different experimental conditions and platforms. The method addresses technical variability and enhances the comparability of data, which is critical for accurate spatial domain identification and boundary preservation. By standardizing heterogeneous datasets, the analysis sets a solid foundation for advanced denoising, multi-section alignment, and eventually, 3D tissue reconstruction.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly 9 computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, using a draft–critique–synthesis workflow and emitting specific JSON artifacts.

steps.title: Draft spatial analysis proposal set
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis-oriented agent to generate an initial set of exactly 9 candidate computational spatial-omics analysis proposals, grounded solely in the provided background about spatially resolved transcriptomics, domain learning, denoising, cross-section integration, and 3D organization. Save them in `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` as a JSON object with top-level key `proposals`, where each item contains only `title` and a detailed `summary`, without executing any analysis or referencing plan templates as analyses.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated hypothesis-generation agent is best suited to synthesize plausible, diverse candidate analyses consistent with the described scientific context, while strictly adhering to the required file format and avoiding premature commitment to final wording.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is explicitly designed to generate draft proposal sets and to write hypotheses/draft_proposals.json, matching the required draft proposal artifact and content for this step.

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Use the Critic-style agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and the public background, and produce a structured critique in `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` that assesses each draft proposal for relevance to spatial domain accuracy, boundary preservation, denoising behavior, cross-section integration, and 3D organization, noting redundancies, gaps, and clarity issues without altering the draft file.
steps.reasoning: A separate critic agent can systematically evaluate coverage and coherence of the draft proposals against the scientific goals, providing explicit guidance for refinement while keeping critique outputs clearly separated in their own artifact.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is specialized for review-only critique of candidate spatial paper analyses and writes hypotheses/critique.json, exactly matching the critique artifact and evaluative role required in this step.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis-oriented agent again to integrate `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, revising, merging, or rewording as needed to produce `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json`. This final file must be a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly 9 items, each with only `title` and a detailed `summary`, representing the refined set of computational spatial-omics analyses most consistent with the hidden paper, without executing any of the analyses or attempting to locate the paper.
steps.reasoning: A final synthesis step is required to transform the critiqued draft into a single coherent, non-redundant set of 9 proposals in the exact schema and path requested, ensuring that the outputs reflect both the initial ideas and the critic’s feedback.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is responsible for synthesizing and finalizing proposal sets and can write hypotheses/final_proposals.json, making it the appropriate agent to integrate the draft and critique into the required final proposal JSON.

provenance.justification: Available templates (e.g., for GO enrichment, cell annotation, or spatial deconvolution) target concrete bioinformatics workflows, whereas this task is a meta-level proposal generation, critique, and synthesis process; therefore, a custom three-step plan tailored to hypothesis and critic agents was created instead of reusing analysis-specific templates.
